Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Torres (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (Redwood CSM); Emma Ford (NorthLight Head of MLOps), Daniel Park (Infra), Sara Liu (CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete):
NorthLight is planning a renewal with a capacity uplift and wants to onboard EU region + private VPC pilot. They are concerned about latency at P95, SOC2 controls, and contract term. Redwood to send tiered pricing and run a 48-hour benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um quick check — can folks hear me ok?
[00:03] Emma Ford: yes — i can hear you, hi maya, thanks.
[00:05] Rafael Torres: morning / afternoon all, rafael here from redwood se.
[00:09] Sara Liu: hey, sara on my side. we're good.
[00:12] Maya Chen: awesome. high level agenda — renewal terms, capacity uplift needs, EU region activation, private/vpc constraints, security checklist, and then next steps. if anything else throw it in.
[00:21] Emma Ford: perfect. we'll start with our constraints — so our platform is live in us-west now. Typical daytime TPS is around 120 reqs/s, tokens per request vary a lot, we're seeing spikes up to 700k tokens per hour, monthly average about 1.8B tokens. Main thing: p95 latency target for user-facing features is below 600ms. right now we're seeing p95 at about 580 with redwood hosted, which is close but we need headroom.
[00:45] Daniel Park: also, we need eu region for data residency. legal requires eu processing for certain customers, and the plan is to route eu traffic to eu nodes. we want to test private vpc because there are firewall rules and onprem connectivity concerns.
[01:05] Rafael Torres: makes sense. to confirm, are you asking for dedicated capacity in EU or a private deployment within your VPC?
[01:10] Emma Ford: preferably dedicated capacity in EU initially then a private vpc pilot if the compliance team signs off. timeline is tight — renewal is end of month so we'd like alignment in two weeks.
[01:20] Nina Patel: got it. maya i'll note that they want the eu dedicated then private pilot.
[01:24] Maya Chen: ok on the renewal side, we can do a one-year extension with tiered pricing (base commit + burst) or a two-year with deeper discounts. i'll send sample amendments. question: do you have a preference on commitment size?
[01:37] Emma Ford: we're thinking about a 35% uplift on committed GPUs — maybe start there and have burst credits. we need guaranteed throughput during peak windows — that's the ask.
[01:46] Rafael Torres: technically we can allocate a dedicated pool in eu region and reserve a warm standby for burst. there will be an SLA spec for throughput and latency. small caveat: when cold-starting large models in a new region there's a short warmup. we typically pre-warm KV caches for canary traffic.
[02:07] Daniel Park: is pre-warming automated? our ops team needs repeatable steps for failover.
[02:12] Rafael Torres: yes we can provide automation. we'll share runbooks. some model variants and quantization choices change warmup times.
[02:20] Sara Liu: security — we need SOC 2 type II evidence, SSO (SAML/SCIM), RBAC, and customer-managed KMS support. can you support HSM/KMS integrations?
[02:33] Maya Chen: yes we support KMS integrations and SAML just fine; we also provide audit logs. i'll attach the security pack after the call. we are SOC 2 compliant, the report is available under NDA.
[02:45] Emma Ford: great. also data retention — can we set retention policies per route? for dev we don't need to keep logs longer than a week, prod we keep 1 year.
[02:56] Nina Patel: we have per-route retention config in console, and we can scope the retention in the private deployment too.
[03:02] Maya Chen: quick dig into benchmarks — rafael, do you have notes from the last throughput runs with their config?
[03:07] Rafael Torres: yeah, i pulled the dev logs. with their current model mix (mix of 7B variants and a custom 13B fine-tune) we saw avg token cost of X and p95 latency of about 580 in us-west under a 24h run. if we move to eu dedicated of same size we expect similar numbers but need to validate NVlink topology and kernel selection.
[03:34] Emma Ford: the 13B fine-tune is sensitive. we can't accept large regressions in quality for cheaper quantization. any quantization plan must be validated against our eval set.
[03:45] Rafael Torres: understood — we'll run quality-controlled evals pre/post quantization and share the prompt set redwood used. we'll also keep a fallback model family in the routing policy.
[03:57] Daniel Park: pricing question — if we go with two-year commit, what's the uplift/discount delta?
[04:02] Maya Chen: ballpark: 12-month commit gives base price, 24-month we'd typically offer 18-22% discount across compute units depending on commitment level. i'll put concrete numbers in the spreadsheet.
[04:14] Sara Liu: are there any egress or data transfer fees between us and eu nodes?
[04:18] Maya Chen: intra-region routing is free for traffic bound to that region; cross-region fallbacks can incur egress depending on the contract. we'll call that out explicitly.
[04:28] Emma Ford: operationally we want a cromwell? (laughs) sorry, i mean runbook for disaster recovery — sequence of failovers and dns TTLs.
[04:36] Rafael Torres: yes we'll share runbook and suggest DNS TTLs and canary rollout cadence.
[04:40] Maya Chen: ok next, timeline: we heard renewal by end of month, eu region activation + dedicated pool within 4-6 weeks post-signature, private vpc pilot targeted in 8-10 weeks. do those windows align?
[04:52] Daniel Park: 4-6 weeks is ok, but the security team requires the private pilot to be before the eu full cutover for some customers. is that feasible?
[04:59] Rafael Torres: we can parallelize pre-work: while dedicated pool is provisioning in eu, we can start network peering and Test VPC connectivity. private pilot full activation is contingent on customer UAT and firewall approvals.
[05:14] Sara Liu: regarding contract terms, we need indemnity clauses for data residency and a clause for third-party audit access. our legal team will send markups.
[05:24] Maya Chen: understood — we'll pass your legal's markups to our legal ops and try to reconcile quickly.
[05:28] Emma Ford: ok, now on benchmarks — can we run a 48-hour load test in your staging with our traffic profile? we want to capture p95, p99 and token throughput and cost per 1M tokens.
[05:40] Rafael Torres: yes, we can run that. we will need their spec file and a service account for test harness. prefer we run it next week.
[05:50] Emma Ford: we'll aim to provide the profile by monday.
[05:53] Maya Chen: great. i'll also include cost modeling for the proposed uplift and burst credits.
[05:59] Daniel Park: small ask: can we get a simple CSV of historical quota utilization and cold-start incidents over the past 90 days? that'll help sizing.
[06:09] Nina Patel: we can surface that in the console for you; i'll coordinate with support to export.
[06:14] Emma Ford: thanks.
[06:16] (Interruption — brief pause while someone mutes/unmutes)
[06:24] Sara Liu: one more technical — we use mTLS internally; does the private deployment support client certs for service-to-service?
[06:32] Rafael Torres: yes for private we support mTLS, plus optional sidecar patterns if you need. we'll include config examples.
[06:39] Maya Chen: ok wrapping up, recap: redwood will send a renewal amendment with tiered pricing and two-year option, security pack (SOC2 + KMS + SAML docs), and benchmark plan. northlight will share traffic profile, latency targets, firewall rules, and legal markups. plan a 48-hour benchmark next week and schedule private pilot kickoff for week of 2026-07-19.
[07:02] Emma Ford: that matches our notes. who will own the pilot kickoff meeting?
[07:06] Maya Chen: rafael will lead the technical kickoff, nina will own post-sales coordination, maya will handle contract and pricing.
[07:12] Rafael Torres: i'll prepare the benchmark harness and pre-checklist.
[07:16] Daniel Park: can you add a short bulleted checklist to the kickoff invite so our infra team can validate ports and peering ahead of time?
[07:23] Nina Patel: yep will do.
[07:25] Maya Chen: any open questions?
[07:27] Sara Liu: none from me, thanks.
[07:29] Emma Ford: no. thanks everyone.
[07:31] Maya Chen: thanks all — i'll follow up with the docs and pricing. talk soon.
